title: Polynomial-size split closures in fixed dimension
formal: Editorial bit-size variant: for each fixed dimension d≥3, does a polynomial p_d exist such that the split closure of every rational polyhedron P in R^d has a rational inequality description of total binary encoding length at most p_d(L), where L is the encoding length of the supplied inequality description of P?
definitions:
Let \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R^d:Ax\le b\}\), with rational A,b explicitly encoded by binary numerators and positive denominators; L includes all entries and dimensions. P may be empty, unbounded or lower dimensional. For \(\pi\in\mathbb Z^d\setminus\{0\}\) and k∈Z define \[P^{\pi,k}=\overline{\operatorname{conv}}\big((P\cap\{\pi^{\mathsf T}x\le k\})\cup(P\cap\{\pi^{\mathsf T}x\ge k+1\})\big).\]The split closure is \(\operatorname{SC}(P)=\bigcap_{\pi,k}P^{\pi,k}\). The bar denotes closure in Euclidean space; the convex hull of an empty set is empty. All d coordinates are integer-constrained for the purpose of the split disjunctions.

A description of size S consists of finitely many rational linear inequalities in the original d variables, with the sum of binary lengths of all coefficients, right-hand sides and delimiters at most S. Extended formulations with extra variables are excluded. The requested polynomial may depend on fixed d but not on the input. Only existence of a description is asked; no algorithm to construct it is required. This bit-size convention is an explicit choice refining the imported phrase polynomial size.
answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked polynomial bound for every fixed d≥3, or disprove it in some fixed dimension by a family requiring superpolynomial total description length. A bound solely on the number of inequalities, without coefficient-size control, is insufficient for this variant.
context: Basu, Conforti, Di Summa and Jiang establish polynomial-size split closures in dimension two. The card asks whether a corresponding size guarantee persists at every fixed higher dimension.
why: This asks whether a standard cutting-plane closure retains a compact representation in fixed dimension.

import_provenance.original_title: Polynomial-size split closures in fixed dimension
import_provenance.original_statement: For each fixed dimension d≥3, does the split closure of a rational polyhedron admit an inequality description polynomial in the binary length of the original description? The split closure intersects all cuts obtained from integer disjunctions a·x≤b or a·x≥b+1; this extends Conforti and collaborators’ positive planar result.
import_provenance.supplied_caveat: Remark: Dimension2 is already settled; polynomial-time integer optimization in fixed dimension does not by itself bound the size of this particular closure.
